title: How the Voynich Manuscript was created
summary: Timm studies how similarly spelled glyph groups are related and where they occur in the manuscript. He argues the text was generated by copying already written glyph groups from nearby text and modifying them (adding, deleting or replacing glyphs), so that the groups only behave like words. The paper is an observational analysis of the transcription with comparisons to a Latin and an English text; it does not fit or score a generator on held-out text.
established: Similarly spelled glyph groups occur with similar frequencies and tend to occur near each other; the paper groups the vocabulary into a few series (around daiin, ol and chedy in EVA) linked by single-glyph changes.
The number of words repeated from one line to the next is raised for consecutive lines in the manuscript, an increase the paper does not find in its Latin and English comparison texts.

The second glyph group of a line is shorter than the first in 48% of lines and longer in 32%, which the paper explains by glyphs added to line-initial groups (and gallows added to paragraph-initial groups), after Vogt's observation that line-initial words are longer than average.
The paper reports that repeated sequences of more than five words are missing from the manuscript and argues that the copying method explains this together with the constantly changing vocabulary.
From spelling variants that do not appear on pages already completed, the paper argues that the pages in Currier B were written after those in Currier A.

open.question: Does a copy-and-modify procedure fitted on public pages only reproduce the manuscript's raised word repetition between consecutive lines and its longer line-initial words on held-out pages?
open.check: a model.json with copy and position components, or a fact attack with generated text

open.question: Is the cross-line repetition the paper describes larger in the manuscript than in natural-language texts of matched size and layout, measured on hidden pages?
open.check: a fact.json comparing a repetition statistic against reference languages

open.question: Do Currier B pages contain spelling variants absent from Currier A pages but not the reverse, as the paper's ordering argument requires?
